title: Cross-functional experiments playbook (canary + A/B) - draft
content:
Purpose:
This working playbook captures a pragmatic cross-functional approach for running canaries, progressive rollouts, and A/B experiments across Redwood’s Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. It’s intentionally informal — a single place for engineers, product, SRE, data, and CS to align on guardrails and practical run-steps during rolling changes and experiments.

High-level goals:
- Minimize customer impact during feature and model changes.
- Detect regressions early (quality, latency, cost, reliability).
- Make rollouts reproducible and auditable across teams.
- Provide a clear escalation path and rollback criteria.

Scope:
- Applies to: model version upgrades, runtime changes (serving runtime flags, kernel selection), routing/policy changes, UI changes that affect API shape, and new telemetry-enabled features.
- Excludes: database migrations that require schema changes (see infra DB migration guide).

Owners & Roles (practical):
- Release Lead (product or PM): coordinates stakeholders, signs off on go/no-go checkpoints.
- Tech Lead (ENG): owns the rollout commands, feature flags, and PRs.
- SRE / Oncall: validates infra health, latency SLOs, and executes rollbacks if threshold breaches.
- Data / Experimentation: defines primary/secondary metrics, runs statistical analysis, and publishes experiment report.
- Solutions / CS: monitors top customers for signals and surfaces qualitative feedback.
- Security/Compliance: briefed when release touches private deployments or KMS/Audit surfaces.

Experiment & Canary taxonomy (working definitions):
- Canary (safety-first): small fraction of real traffic running a new change. Primary purpose: detect catastrophic regressions. Short-lived (minutes to hours).
- Progressive rollout: staged traffic ramps (e.g., 1% → 10% → 50%) with gating checks at each step.
- A/B experiment: controlled split to evaluate product/quality deltas. Requires pre-registered metrics and analysis plan. Longer-lived (hours to weeks).
- Dark-launch: traffic routed to new variant but results not returned to users; used for telemetry-only validation.

Signal checklist (what we watch):
- Safety & correctness: error rate (5xx), request rejections, model failures, functional unit tests failing in prod traces.
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 server-side + end-to-end customer-perceived latency.
- Cost/per-token: billing anomalies (tokens per request jump), GPU / pod CPU utilization.
- Quality: primary model quality metric (prompt-set pass rate, BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, or task-specific accuracy).
- Customer impact: top-customer error reports, session abandonment, support tickets.
- Telemetry integrity: missing logs, dropped spans, metrics discontinuities.

Metric definitions (examples to copy into experiments):
- primary_metric = "median-inference-latency-ms" (lower is better)
- safety_metric = "5xx-percentage" (threshold default: >0.5% triggers rollback)
- quality_metric = "eval-prompt-pass-rate" (relative delta of >= -2.0% flagged)
- cost_metric = "tokens-per-call" (spikes >20% flagged)

Pre-launch checklist (quick scan):
- [ ] Experiment definition doc exists and linked (metrics, hypothesis, analysis window).
- [ ] Runbook & rollback steps authored and owners assigned.
- [ ] Monitoring dashboards created and tested (templated dashboard link).
- [ ] Canary variant implements telemetry for all primary metrics.
- [ ] Feature flagging config present in code + console (can target by region/account).
- [ ] Load and safety tests run in staging with representative load.
- [ ] Legal/security checklist reviewed for private deployments.

Canary sizing & traffic allocation (practical defaults):
- Immediate smoke canary: 0.1% global traffic or 1 node pool (min 5 requests/min) for 15–60 minutes. Purpose: detect hard failures.
- Short canary: 1% traffic for 30–120 minutes (sensitive to low-volume customers; if traffic low, target specific test accounts).
- Ramp canary sequence: 1% → 5% → 25% → 100% with gating checks at each step. Typical dwell: 30–120 minutes per step for Hosted; longer for Dedicated/private where SLAs require thorough checks.
- A/B sample size guidance: run power analysis (Data team helper). As a rule-of-thumb, for small effect sizes on quality metrics, plan for multi-day runs or explicit sample-targeted targeting.

Gating checks and thresholds (defaults — teams may tighten):
- Block/rollback if safety_metric delta > +0.3 percentage points relative to baseline OR absolute safety_metric > 0.5%.
- Block/rollback if primary_metric p95 increases > +100 ms and sustained over analysis window.
- Flag if quality_metric falls by >= 1.5% relative (investigate before rollback unless simultaneously other signals indicate severe customer impact).
- Cost spike: tokens-per-call > +20% sustained for 30m.
- Any critical customer (enterprise with support-tier) reports functional regressions: immediate rollback and oncall notify.

Monitoring & dashboards (must-haves):
- Canary overview: traffic allocation, variant ids, start time, owner, current step.
- Latency heatmap (region x model-version).
- Error breakdown (5xx by endpoint/variant).
- Cost telemetry (tokens/call, GPU utilization, infra spend rate).
- Quality probes: synthetic prompt set pass rate trend and CI bands.
- Alert Router: which alerts page SRE vs oncall lead vs product.

Runbook — immediate incident steps (short):
1) Pause ramp: set feature-flag to previous variant or reduce traffic to 0% for canary.
2) Notify: ping #prod-rollouts, product lead, and oncall.
3) Triage: collect traces, logs, model server metrics, recent deploy/PR list.
4) If revertable flag/PR exists, revert or flip flag. If not, initiate emergency rollback playbook (infra-led).
5) Post-mortem owner assigned within 24 hours.

Communication plan (cross-functional):
- During canary: short status updates posted to the rollout Slack thread every checkpoint (1%, 5%, 25%, 100%).
- On issues: immediate page + short incident summary in thread.
- Post-rollout: publish a short 1-paragraph result + link to experiment notebook and dataset.

A/B experiment specifics (working guidance):
- Pre-registration required: hypothesis, primary/secondary metrics, analysis window, segmentation, and stopping rules.
- Randomization: deterministic assignment via request ID hashing + experiment salt. Document mapping logic in PR.
- Exposure logging: record experiment_id, variant, and relevant model metadata in the request logs.
- Data latency: expect 30–120 minute lag for aggregated metrics — plan analysis windows accordingly.
- Statistical testing: use pre-approved tests from Data team. Don’t peek frequently; use pre-specified stopping rules or sequential testing methods documented in experiment doc.

Example short experiment spec (copyable):
- name: "rerank-new-loss-ab-2026-02"
- hypothesis: "New reranker increases click-through for short queries by >= 3% without increasing latency > 50ms"
- primary_metric: "ctr-short-queries"
- secondary_metrics: ["median-inference-latency-ms", "5xx-percentage"]
- sample_size_estimate: "see linked power analysis"
- start_date: 2026-02-15
- end_date: 2026-03-01
- owner: "Diego Martínez"

Data quality & analysis notes:
- Ensure consistent deduping logic between logging and analytics. We had one prior data drift where request_id changed at the edge and doubled impressions — watch for header transformations in edge proxies.
- Keep raw event logs for at least 30 days for debug; aggregated experiment snapshots for 1 year where permitted.

Common pitfalls / unresolved questions (TODOs):
- How to consistently gate private deployments where traffic is low — recommend synthetic traffic harness and targeted test accounts.
- We still need a single canonical dashboard template that teams can instantiate from the Console with one click.
- Define exact alert thresholds for Dedicated customers with custom SLAs (SRE + Account team to own).
- Need automation to flip flags on a timed schedule and to rollback automatically when threshold breached (epic: ROLL-AUTO).

Templates & quick snippets:
- Rollout Slack message (checkpoint): "[ROLLOUT] reranker-v4 — step=5% — owner=@ava — p95=210ms (+8ms) — 5xx=0.12% — status=ok"
- Immediate rollback message: "[ROLLBACK] reranker-v4 — stop ramp — rollback to reranker-v3 — reason=safety_metric spike to 0.87% — actioned=@sre_oncall"

Postmortem / experiment write-up (minimum):
- Summary (1 paragraph)
- Key metrics and graphs (link)
- Root cause or explanation for observed deltas
- Action items (owners + ETA)
- Knowledge check: is this safe to enable for Dedicated/Private?

Appendix — short historical notes (for context):
- 2025-04: incident where a kernel change increased p99 by 600ms for edge sequences; root cause: wrong quantization kernel selected for longer sequences (led to new kernel-selection tests).
- 2025-11: spike in tokens-per-call due to a prompt-template change — added tokens-per-call to default canary watchlist.

Notes to self (informal):
- We should run a workshop with SRE/data/product to cement thresholds — keep this doc alive and move to Confluence once we stabilize defaults.
- Consider a small "rollout lab" where teams can practice forced rollbacks on a staging fleet.

---
Working copy, not authoritative. Copy into a Confluence page and fill the TODOs once we converge.
